summary: Wrote and ran /app/backend/tests/test_fix8_structured_portion.py — 17 tests covering the Fix 8 architectural change (structured portion + code-owned arithmetic + hallucination fallback + preview envelope + subscription gate). 16/17 pass. The 1 failing test documents a RESIDUAL BUG: for the user's exact 'High Protein Yogurt' scenario, `_lookup_reference` picks the wrong reference ('protein powder' 400/80/10/3.3) because its longest-substring rule matches 'protein' (7 chars) before 'yogurt' (6 chars) in the food name. Result: hallucination guard sees max_div=90% (<100% threshold) and does NOT fall back, so the model's bad 138cal/100g × 2 = 276cal is returned — the user's original bug is NOT eliminated for label names containing the word 'protein'. Also flagged a Fix-1 vs Fix-8 tension: label yogurts have food-specific Atwater factors so the printed 62cal/100g reconciles down to 53cal (P*4+C*4+F*9), meaning the structured path's 124cal/200g becomes 107cal/200g after the final sanitize step. 109/113 existing tests still pass; 2 pre-existing failures in test_food_analyze_preview.py are subscription-gate related (unrelated to Fix 8).

critical.issue: RESIDUAL: user's original yogurt bug is NOT fixed by Fix 8 for food names containing 'protein'. `_lookup_reference('High Protein Yogurt')` returns the 'protein powder' macros (400cal/80P/10C/3.3F per 100g) instead of 'yogurt' (59/10/4/0.4). Hallucination guard then computes max_divergence=90% (<100% threshold) so fallback never fires. Bad model per_100g = 138/31/1/1 flows through unchanged → 276cal / 62P / 2C / 2F at 200g portion. Fix: bias `_lookup_reference` toward the LAST/rightmost token match, or add explicit alias 'high protein yogurt'→'greek yogurt' / 'protein yogurt'→'greek yogurt', or lower `detect_hallucination` threshold from >100% to >50% divergence. File: /app/backend/server.py:8135-8161 (_lookup_reference) and :8413-8435 (detect_hallucination).

Fix-1 vs Fix-8 interaction: structured path deterministically computes 124cal at 200g yogurt (62×2), then the FINAL `sanitize_food_entry` reconciles it DOWN to 107cal because the label's 62cal/100g exceeds the P*4+C*4+F*9=53.4 derivation by 13.9% (>12% label tolerance). User's own spec says 124 is correct. Options: (a) skip Fix-1 reconciliation on the structured path when energy_source=='label' and per_100g_source in ('label','retry_label'); (b) widen label tolerance to 20%; (c) only reconcile calories, never derive down when user provided portion_g. File: /app/backend/server.py:8213 and :8750.

minor.issue: `_extract_portion_grams` interprets '1 cup' as 240g, so a label with serving_size='1 cup' + per-serving totals is auto-derived into per_100g rather than raising 422. Depending on desired behaviour, either accept that (helpful default) or restrict derive_per_100g to explicit gram serving_sizes.

Pre-existing (not Fix 8): tests in test_food_analyze_preview.py fail because the subscription gate now returns 403 before the image-size/400-validation runs, so those older tests using random unseeded user_ids assert wrong status codes.

action_items: Fix `_lookup_reference` so 'High Protein Yogurt' maps to greek yogurt, not protein powder. Add alias entries and/or prefer rightmost/head-noun matches over longest substring.

Decide the Fix-1 vs Fix-8 policy: when the structured path owns the arithmetic on a label per_100g, either skip the final calorie reconciliation, widen tolerance for yogurt-like Atwater deltas, or accept the reconciled value as the new source of truth.
Consider lowering detect_hallucination threshold from >100% to >50% divergence — a 90% delta on the yogurt scenario is clearly invented but slips through the current guard.
Reseed test users for /app/backend/tests/test_food_analyze_preview.py so subscription gate doesn't 403 them before validation fires (pre-existing test rot).

server.py:8750 final `sanitize_food_entry(_scaled, portion_g=_portion_applied)` on the structured path second-guesses the deterministic label × portion arithmetic that the whole Fix 8 architecture was built to protect.

If main agent widens Fix-1 label tolerance instead of skipping reconciliation, update ARCHETYPES yogurt expected_cal from 53/96/107 back to 62/112/124.
rca_of_issue: USER BUG RCA — the Fix 8 architecture (structured portion + code-owned arithmetic + hallucination fallback) is CORRECTLY implemented and does eliminate portion-math errors. BUT the user's exact yogurt bug is NOT fixed because `_lookup_reference` (server.py:8135) picks the wrong reference food for label names containing the word 'protein'. It normalizes 'High Protein Yogurt' → 'high protein yogurt', then iterates INGREDIENT_MACROS looking for the LONGEST substring key. 'protein' (7 chars, maps to protein powder 400/80/10/3.3) beats 'yogurt' (6 chars, maps to greek yogurt 59/10/4/0.4). detect_hallucination(model_per_100g={138,31,1,1}, ref={400,80,10,3.3}) computes max_div = |1-3.3|/max(3.3,1)=70% and |138-400|/400=66% and |31-80|/80=61% and |1-10|/10=90% → max_div=0.9 which is <1.0 → NOT flagged as hallucination → fallback never fires → model's 138cal/100g × 2 = 276cal returned to user. Fix path: add explicit alias 'high protein yogurt'→'greek yogurt', OR change lookup to prefer the last matching token, OR lower detect_hallucination threshold to >0.5. Reproduction: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_fix8_structured_portion.py::test_yogurt_hallucination_falls_back_to_reference -v. Mitigation: any of the three approaches above.
